item.text:
**Verdict:** No.

The 2023 record does not show Putin protecting political equality in any meaningful sense. The strongest evidence is that minorities, women, indigenous people, LGBT+ people, opposition regions, and antiwar or unpopular viewpoints remained structurally disadvantaged, while the regime used central control, discriminatory mobilization, and sham elections in occupied territories. The only pro-side evidence is formal: women and minority groups were not legally barred from participation.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Short claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Russia: 2023 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices | U.S. Department of State | 22 Apr 2024 | [link](https://www.state.gov/reports/2023-country-reports-on-human-rights-practices/russia) | The report says no laws formally limited participation of women and minority groups, and they did participate. But it also says women were only about 18% of elected seats, ethnic Russians dominated the political and administrative system, and authorities restricted political participation and organized sham elections in occupied Ukrainian territories. This is weak formal counterevidence only. | 4B.7, 4B.2, 4B.3 |
| Russia: Freedom in the World 2023 Country Report | Freedom House | 2023 | [link](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2023) | Freedom House says women are underrepresented in politics, national minority regions are tightly controlled, some republics do not have direct gubernatorial elections, and LGBT+ people face major barriers. It also says the state targeted minority groups and kept politics dominated by ethnic Russians. | 4B.7, 4B.4, 4B.5 |
| Russia: Nations in Transit 2023 Country Report | Freedom House | 2023 | [link](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/nations-transit/2023) | Freedom House says Russia’s political leadership and ruling coalition embraced an isolationist, militant vision, local autonomy was curbed, and ethnic minority regions were more visible targets of discrimination and central control during the war. It also notes the remaining local opposition space was shrinking, not protected. | 4B.7, 4B.4, 4B.5 |
| Russia: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report | Freedom House | 2024 | [link](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2024) | Looking back at 2023, Freedom House says ethnic and racial minority groups and their home regions were disproportionately targeted in mobilization, while LGBT+ rights worsened further. This is direct evidence against political equality for excluded groups. | 4B.7, 3B.7, 4B.5 |
| Russia: Nations in Transit 2024 Country Report | Freedom House | 2024 | [link](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/nations-transit/2024) | Looking back at 2023, Freedom House says local autonomy had eroded, electoral integrity worsened, and municipal space was shrinking and tightly controlled. That is evidence against protection of opposition regions and unpopular viewpoints, even where some local councils remained a thin opposition training ground. | 4B.7, 4B.2, 4B.4, 4B.5 |

**Search gap:** I found no credible 2023 evidence that Putin actively protected political equality for minorities, women, excluded groups, opposition regions, or unpopular viewpoints. The best counterevidence is only formal legal participation, not substantive equal treatment.
